text:
Artyom Levshunov, the second overall pick in 2024, is playing 20:29 a night for Chicago, and the scoresheet hasn't paid him back. He has three points in 22 games and has gone 14 straight without one.

Some of that is bad luck. Chicago has scored 6.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of gap that usually swings back. But not all of it: over his last ten games the chances with him on have thinned out too (7.9 on-ice expected goals, the quality of chances, against 9.6 usual), and at five on five the Blackhawks get only 39.7% of the expected goals when he plays.

Context matters for a 21-year-old on a rebuilding team. Evolving-Hockey had his teammates in the bottom 3% by impact last season, which drags down raw numbers, though it also had opponents' chances piling up with him out there. The comparisons are kinder than the stat line: Victor Hedman and Drew Doughty, both second overall picks, scored 0.27 and 0.33 points a game in their first full seasons. Watch the defensive numbers before the points.
headline: Artyom Levshunov is playing big minutes without the points
